πολεμίων ἤδη καθῃρημένου. τεῖχος οὖν ἐνταῦθα βασιλεύς τε καὶ ἄρχοντες καὶ ὅσοι
δυνάμει ταύτην περι τειχίζοντες, οὓς ἀξιοῖ χέειν μετανοίας ἀδιάλειπτα δάκρυα , ἃ
τοῖς ὁρῶσι διὰ παντὸς προξενεῖ πεπτωκός. ταῦτα, φησίν, ὑπάρχει αὐτοῖς, καὶ εἰ μὴ
πάλιν τὴν λύπην σημαίνει τῆς πάλαι φρουρούσης δυνά μεως, ὑπερβολικῶς τοῦτο
δηλῶν. «ἐν θλίψει δέ», λέγει, «τοῦ κυρίου ἐμνήσθησαν ἐξ ὅλης τῆς καρδίας». τοῦτο
τοίνυν ποιήσατε, φησί, νυκτὸς καὶ ἡμέρας δακρύοντες καὶ «ἐπὶ ταῖς κοίταις ὑμῶν
κατα νύγητε»· μηδὲ νῆψιν ἡγεῖσθε τὴν ἀπὸ τούτων ἀπαλλαγήν· μετάνοια γὰρ εἰς
σωτηρίαν ἐστίν. νήφει δέ τις οὐκ ἀγαθῶν, ἀλλὰ χειρόνων παυόμενος. τῷ δὲ νῷ
συνάπτου διὰ παντὸς πρὸς Χριστόν, ὅπως σε φυλάξειεν ὡς κόρην ὀφθαλμοῦ καί σοι
τεῖχος γένηται. 60 Προσεκτικὸν ἡ νύξ, συστρεφομένης ἐν αὐτῇ τῆς ψυχῆς ἐν τῇ τῶν
αἰσθήσεων ἠρεμίᾳ. τότε κελεύει μελετᾶν ἐν ταῖς ἐντολαῖς τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ λέγειν μετὰ

pass_a_gloss: Hostile forces are now dismantled. Thus, a defensive line stands—king, leaders, all mighty defenders encircling this site—whom he judges fit to shed endless tears of contrition, tears that, to observers, ever signal collapse. He affirms these as theirs; if not renewing the sign of former guard’s grief, he overstates it. “In anguish,” he declares, “they recalled the Lord with full hearts.” So act, he urges: mourn day and night, weeping on couches; deem not freedom from this as clarity—repentance brings deliverance. True watchfulness turns from evil, not pursues good. Bind your thoughts constantly to Christ, that he shield you like an eye’s pupil and be your bulwark. Night is vigilant, as the soul rests within it, senses stilled. Then he bids: practice God’s decrees, chant with David: “In bed, my heart pondered; my spirit burned.” With night split into four guards, utter David’s line: “My eyes forestalled the watches”; with Habakkuk: “I’ll take my post on the watchtower, scan, await the Lord’s word in me, his reply to my plea.” Then you’ll declare: “He’ll proclaim peace over his folk.” Hence, muse quietly in this era’s night; for your struggle isn’t versus blood and flesh, but versus authorities, dominions. “Indeed, you ignore when the household master arrives—late, midnight, cockcrow, or dawn.” Do not assume the thief arrives suddenly and finds you asleep; if you knew his watch, you’d stay awake and not let him dig through your house. Again: raise your hands to him via good works. The contest isn’t over trifles but from lacking grasp of divine speech, making your little ones fail and stand at the start of all powers—the eleven commands of God—unable to progress without God’s help and the bread that upholds the heart. After the prophet urged, Jerusalem obeyed and told God: “Don’t turn your face from me,” “Look on me and pity me,” “Don’t reproach me in your anger, nor chasten me in your rage.” The plague exceeds human kind. I know I broke the law and lie under later penalties, including: “You’ll eat your children’s flesh.” I took them as threats till I learned, Lord, “your law is true.” Still, as priest and prophet, I didn’t hear of the killing in the temple’s heart. On earth lay all who, from age, can’t bear toil—a sad sight, like youth and virgin slaughter not being enough, wishing even these killings led out before a more bitter life. Land’s exports are life’s needs, where they slept unwatchful and unpraying, locking soul’s eyes from sin and folly. Who are these? If they’re little ones, Not strange that those once virtuous and strong in war now lie helpless before foes. You end their false peace and shatter their wicked schemes. Judah’s fugitives, who fled to me for safety, are gone—none left—because of your wrath on them. Their sins made mighty foes rise. Before the city fell, the prophet saw ruin: he hid, poor, as the Lord taught. Yet he still lacked good, having tested them, saying, “All day I was mocked,” and sharing their pain. He quotes David: “Death’s shadow covered me.” When he seems to ease their toil, he returns, punishing without cease. “All the day” means daily war, as David sang. It shows he turned his hand—once giving me good, now sending discipline—like a changed grip. Our treachery from sin is shown.
pass_b_english:
The enemies have already been stripped bare. Therefore, here a wall is formed by the king and the rulers and all who, in power, surround this place with fortifications—those whom he deems worthy to pour out unceasing tears of repentance, tears which, to those who see them, constantly present a fallen state. These things, he says, belong to them; and if he does not again signify the sorrow of the formerly guarding power, he does so hyperbolically. “In distress,” he says, “they remembered the Lord from their whole heart.” Therefore, do this, he says: weep by night and by day, and “upon your beds, lament.” Do not regard the release from these things as sobriety; for repentance is unto salvation. Sobriety, however, belongs not to good things, but to ceasing from worse things. And let your mind be continually joined to Christ, that he may guard you as the pupil of the eye and become a wall for you. The night is watchful, as the soul is gathered within it in the stillness of the senses. Then he commands to meditate upon the commandments of God and to say with David: “By night, with my heart, I meditated; and my spirit was stirred.” And since the night is divided into four watches, say with David: “My eyes anticipated the watches,” and with Habakkuk: “I will stand upon my watch, and set myself upon the tower, and will look forth to see what he will say unto me, and what I shall answer when I am reproved.” For then you shall say: “That he will speak peace unto his people.” Therefore, meditate in silence during the night of this present age; for you do not have “a wrestling against blood and flesh, but against the principalities, against the powers.” “For you know not when the lord of the house comes, at evening, or at midnight, or at the cockcrowing, or in the morning.”

Do not suppose that the thief will come upon you unawares and find you sleeping; for if you knew at what hour the robber would come, you would have stayed awake and would not have allowed your house to be broken into. Moreover, lift up your hands to him through the work of good deeds. The struggle is not about trivial matters, but arises from the lack of understanding of the divine word, causing your little ones to falter and to stand at the beginning of all powers—the eleven commandments of God—being unable to advance without God’s cooperation and without the sustaining bread that strengthens the heart. When the prophet had exhorted, Jerusalem was persuaded and said to God: “Do not turn your face away from me,” “Look upon me and have mercy on me,” “Do not rebuke me in your anger, nor discipline me in your wrath.” The wound is greater than human nature. I know that I have transgressed the law and am subject to the ensuing penalties, among which is the statement: “You shall eat the fruit of your womb, the flesh of your sons and your daughters.” I once thought these words were merely threats, but Lord, I have come to know that “your law is truth.” Yet, as a priest and prophet, I did not learn of the slaughter taking place in the midst of the sanctuary. Upon the earth lay all those who, due to age, were unable to endure the labors—a pitiable sight, as if the slaughter of youths and virgins were not enough, and even these massacres should be led forth before entering a more bitter life. The exports of the land are the necessities of life, among which they had lain down without keeping watch or praying, having shut the eyes of the soul against sin and folly. And who are these? If they are children,

It is not at all surprising that, even now, before these events, those who seemed to have advanced in virtue and whose entire soul was blameless and capable in warfare have become subject to enemies. Yet you, as a good one, put an end to such a life for them, and you cut short every one of their establishments that is based on evil.

The ones dwelling around me in Judah, he says, who had taken refuge in me, hoping for salvation from this place—none of them remains, due to the anger you have brought upon them. For the very things by which they sinned, many and powerful enemies have now arisen against them.

Terrible things have happened to the prophet even before the city was captured and while it lay in ruins. Therefore, beginning with a different elemental instruction, he hides himself, seeing poverty and desolation in the city through the Lord’s discipline. And yet he himself has not become less in lack of good things, while at the same time having come into circumstances where he examined them, so as to say: “I spent the whole day being mocked,” and at the same time sharing in their terrible misfortunes and the sorrow that arises from compassion.

He also says, according to David: “The shadow of death has fallen upon me.” For when it seems he is giving them a brief respite from their labors, he again turns back and relentlessly pursues them, inflicting continuous punishment.

The phrase “all the day” indicates each day, as David says: “All the day fighting has oppressed me.” It would also suggest that he has turned his hand against them, and that long ago he provided me with good things, but now he brings disciplines upon me, as if he had changed his hand.

The treachery that has befallen us from sin is signified.
